rationale: Ground truth was sparse (LGTM approve, 4 minor org/clarity comments about patch.py provenance, use_all2all kwargs style, and moving two helpers to utils) — neither candidate substantively hits any of these, so recall is low for both. Both independently converge on the same real-looking num_stale_output_tokens double-seed bug (matching file:line citations), which is credible evidence it's grounded rather than fabricated. Y's report is more disciplined: it separates 'validated' (checked, found fine) from 'sweep'/flagged findings, quotes exact code snippets as evidence, and confirms it read the PR-time tree — this lowers fabrication risk. X is more verbose with confident but harder-to-verify claims (exact CI gate colors, precise reproduction counts, '105 passed') that inflate apparent authority without corroboration. Actionability is comparable; X gives slightly more inline fix code, Y gives more precise test-modification asks.
